title: Self-Reciprocity (Palindromy) of Gaussian q-Binomial Coefficients
description: Proves that the Gaussian (q-)binomial coefficient [n choose k]_q, viewed as a polynomial in q, is palindromic (self-reciprocal) of degree k·(n-k). Over a field this is the clean algebraic identity [n,k]_q = q^{k(n-k)}·[n,k]_{q⁻¹}, equivalently that the coefficient sequence reads the same forwards and backwards (a_j = a_{k(n-k)-j}). Adds a Gaussian-polynomial layer over ℤ[X] (q = X): by induction on the q-Pascal recurrence the polynomial qBinom X n k is monic of natDegree k·(n-k), has constant term 1, has nonnegative coefficients, and hence both extreme coefficients are pinned to 1 — the structural scaffolding of Sylvester's coefficient array. This palindromy plus the pinned ends is the symmetric half of Sylvester's theorem (1878) that the coefficient sequence is symmetric and unimodal. The file then goes further: it upgrades palindromy to an integral coefficient-reversal over ℤ[X] (via Polynomial.reflect), adds ring-homomorphism naturality and the q = 1 degeneration to C(n,k), introduces a Unimodal predicate with a general palindrome-plus-rising-first-half criterion, and PROVES unimodality unconditionally for the columns k = 0, 1, 2 (the k = 2 array ⌊j/2⌋+1 being the first genuine rise-then-fall bump) and, via the symmetry [n,k]_q = [n,n−k]_q, for every codimension n−k ≤ 2. It then closes k = 3 completely: a second q-Pascal form gives an exact 0/1 "center-band" recursion across the box-binding peak that a naive induction cannot cross, settling the full first-half monotonicity for k = 3 with NO 𝔰𝔩₂-representation theory or O'Hara decomposition — the box constraint is beaten by elementary parity bookkeeping alone. Combined with the codimension-≤-2 symmetry this gives unimodality for k ≤ 3 or k ≥ n − 3; the open range of Sylvester's theorem is now precisely the interior 4 ≤ k ≤ n − 4 (first open instance: [8,4]_q). Built on the parent's recurrence-defined q-binomial library via both q-Pascal identities. 43 theorems, 1 definition, 0 sorries, 0 axioms — verified.

meta.author: Lean Genius Researcher
meta.assumptions: The reciprocity identity is proved over an arbitrary field R for any nonzero q (invertibility of q is genuinely needed to form q⁻¹ and to cancel q^{k+1}·(q⁻¹)^{k+1} = 1). The Gaussian-polynomial layer (degree, monicity, constant term, coefficient nonnegativity, pinned extreme coefficients) is proved over ℤ[X] with q = X — no field hypothesis there, since it inducts directly on the q-Pascal recurrence over the ordered ring ℤ. No characteristic or positivity hypotheses on R. The underlying q-binomial coefficients are the parent's, defined over an arbitrary commutative ring via the q-Pascal recurrence. #print axioms reports only the foundational propext / Classical.choice / Quot.sound — no sorryAx, no Lean.ofReduceBool.
originalContributions: Machine-checked self-reciprocity (palindromy) of the Gaussian binomial: [n,k]_q = q^{k(n-k)}·[n,k]_{q⁻¹} over an arbitrary field, proved by induction on n using BOTH parent q-Pascal identities (the first for the reflected side, the second for the original)

Identification of the exact algebraic mechanism of palindromy: the reflected recurrence matches the original because expanding the left by the second q-Pascal identity and the reflected right by the first q-Pascal identity produces termwise-equal sides after the cancellation q^{(k+1)(n-k)}·(q⁻¹)^{k+1} = q^{(k+1)(n-k-1)}
Reflected convenience form q^{k(n-k)}·[n,k]_{q⁻¹} = [n,k]_q and an involutivity sanity check confirming the twisted reflection q ↦ q⁻¹ is an involution
Explicit, honestly-scoped separation of the symmetric (palindromy) half of Sylvester's theorem — proved here — from the unimodal half, which remains open

Gaussian-polynomial layer over ℤ[X] (q = X): a single induction on the q-Pascal recurrence proves qBinom X n k is monic with natDegree = k·(n-k) (the X^{k+1}-shifted summand strictly dominates in degree whenever n-k ≥ 1, supplying both the degree and the monic leading term), has constant term 1, and has coefficientwise-nonnegative coefficients

Pinned extreme coefficients: combining monicity (top coefficient at degree k(n-k) equals 1) with the constant-term computation gives qBinom_X_extreme_coeffs — both ends of the coefficient array equal 1 — which together with nonnegativity and palindromy is the exact structural precursor to Sylvester's symmetric-unimodal shape

High-codimension unimodality for free via symmetry: qBinomCoeff_unimodal_of_codim_le_two uses [n,k]_q = [n,n−k]_q (qBinom_symm) to transport the k = 0, 1, 2 base cases to every k with n − k ≤ 2 — an infinite family of high-k columns settled with zero new analysis

Sylvester's theorem CLOSED for k = 3, elementarily: the second q-Pascal form [N+4,3]_q = [N+3,3]_q + q^{N+1}·[N+3,3]_q writes the box-`3×(N+1)` increment as the box-`3×N` increment plus the *exactly known* k = 2 ramp, giving an explicit 0/1 "center-band" recursion across the two or three indices where the box constraint first binds inside the first half — no 𝔰𝔩₂-action (Proctor 1982) or O'Hara injection (1990) is needed for this specific column

The open range of Sylvester's theorem in this file has narrowed from 'all k ≥ 3' to the interior 4 ≤ k ≤ n − 4: qBinomCoeff_unimodal_of_codim_le_three now covers k ≤ 3 or k ≥ n − 3, so the first genuinely open instance is the coefficient array of [8,4]_q

Natural-number arithmetic with truncated subtraction (omega) and the ring tactic on ℕ exponents

overview.historicalContext: The Gaussian binomial coefficient [n choose k]_q was studied by Gauss as the generating polynomial counting k-dimensional subspaces of an n-dimensional vector space over F_q. As a polynomial in q it has degree k(n-k) and nonnegative integer coefficients. In 1878 J. J. Sylvester proved, in the course of his work on invariant theory and the resolution of a conjecture of Cayley, that this coefficient sequence is not merely symmetric but unimodal — it rises to a peak and then falls. The symmetry (palindromy) is elementary and classical; the unimodality is deep. The first fully rigorous proof of unimodality was given by R. Proctor in 1982 using the representation theory of sl₂ (a 'raising/lowering operator' argument), following K. O'Hara's later combinatorial proof (1990). Sylvester's theorem is the prototype for a large family of unimodality results in algebraic combinatorics.
overview.problemStatement: The seeker's open question combinations-formula-oq-03-oq-04 asks to establish unimodality of the Gaussian q-binomial coefficients on top of the parent's q-binomial library. This entry first rigorously formalizes the symmetric precursor — the coefficient sequence is palindromic, stated over a field as [n,k]_q = q^{k(n-k)}·[n,k]_{q⁻¹} and integrally over ℤ[X] as a coefficient-reversal a_j = a_{k(n-k)−j} — and then attacks unimodality directly: it is proved unconditionally for the columns k = 0, 1, 2, extended for free to every codimension n − k ≤ 2 via the symmetry [n,k]_q = [n,n−k]_q, and then closed completely for k = 3 by an elementary "center-band" recursion that tracks the coefficient array exactly (0 or 1 increments) across the box constraint that defeats a naive induction. A general reduction shows that for every fixed k, unimodality follows from weak monotonicity of the array's first half alone; what remains open after this file is that first-half monotonicity for the interior range 4 ≤ k ≤ n − 4, whose only known proofs for general k use an 𝔰𝔩₂-action (Proctor 1982) or an explicit injection between coefficient levels (O'Hara 1990).
overview.proofStrategy: The palindromy identity is proved by induction on n with a case split on k. The boundary cases k=0, the diagonal k=n (both q-binomials equal 1), and k>n (both vanish) are direct. In the generic interior case k<n, the left side [n+1,k+1]_q is expanded by the SECOND q-Pascal identity qBinom_pascal' ([n+1,k+1]_q = q^{n-k}·[n,k]_q + [n,k+1]_q) while the reflected right side [n+1,k+1]_{q⁻¹} is expanded by the FIRST q-Pascal identity qBinom_pascal ([n+1,k+1]_q = [n,k]_q + q^{k+1}·[n,k+1]_q). Substituting the induction hypothesis at (n,k) and (n,k+1) makes the two sides coincide term-by-term: the coefficient of the reflected [n,k]_{q⁻¹} matches after q^{n-k}·q^{k(n-k)} = q^{(k+1)(n-k)}, and the coefficient of [n,k+1]_{q⁻¹} matches after the cancellation q^{(k+1)(n-k)}·(q⁻¹)^{k+1} = q^{(k+1)(n-k-1)}, valid since q ≠ 0.
keyInsights: **Palindromy is the symmetric half of unimodality**: A symmetric unimodal sequence is the conclusion of Sylvester's theorem. The symmetry a_j = a_{k(n-k)-j} — proved here both as the field identity and integrally over ℤ[X] via Polynomial.reflect — is elementary and reduces to the two q-Pascal recurrences. Isolating it turns the remaining problem into 'a symmetric nonnegative array is unimodal', which the general reduction qBinomCoeff_unimodal_of_first_half_mono then further collapses to weak monotonicity of the first half alone.

**Both q-Pascal identities together produce termwise agreement**: The single most important structural fact is that expanding the original by the second q-Pascal identity and the reflection by the first q-Pascal identity yields two expressions that agree coefficient-by-coefficient after collecting powers of q. Using the same Pascal identity on both sides does NOT give a termwise match — the two forms are consistent only because qBinom_pascal and qBinom_pascal' compute the same q-binomial.

**Invertibility of q is essential, not cosmetic**: The reflection substitutes q ↦ q⁻¹ and relies on q^{k+1}·(q⁻¹)^{k+1} = 1, so the identity is naturally a field statement with q ≠ 0. Over a general ring one would instead pass to a polynomial reversal; the field formulation keeps the proof to elementary power arithmetic (pow_add, inv_pow, mul_inv_cancel_left₀).

**Truncated subtraction never bites**: The exponents k(n-k), (k+1)(n-k), and (k+1)(n-k-1) use ℕ subtraction, but the delicate step (writing n-k = (n-k-1)+1) is only taken in the branch k<n where n-k ≥ 1, so the subtraction is exact exactly where it is used; the diagonal and above-diagonal cases are dispatched before any such rewrite.

**The degree comes from the shifted summand, not the sum**: In the q-Pascal recurrence qBinom X (n+1)(k+1) = A + X^{k+1}·B with A = qBinom X n k and B = qBinom X n (k+1), the shifted term X^{k+1}·B has natDegree (k+1)(n-k), strictly above deg A = k(n-k) whenever n-k ≥ 1. So the sum's degree and leading (monic) coefficient are inherited entirely from X^{k+1}·B (degree_add_eq_left_of_degree_lt / Monic.add_of_left after add_comm); the interior induction never needs to reason about a potential cancellation of leading terms. This is the polynomial-over-ℤ[X] counterpart of the field palindromy: the field proof uses q⁻¹, but the coefficient-array structure lives over ℤ and needs no inverses.

**Extreme coefficients are pinned, and the interior is now settled for small k**: Monicity fixes the top coefficient (degree k(n-k)) to 1 and coeff_mul_X_pow' fixes the constant term to 1, so qBinom_X_extreme_coeffs closes both ends of the array. With coefficient nonnegativity and the palindromy this is the symmetric skeleton; the actual rise-then-fall of the interior — Sylvester's unimodality — is then proved outright for k = 0, 1, 2 and reduced, for general k, to a single first-half-monotonicity inequality.

**Unimodality reduces to first-half monotonicity of a symmetric array**: The reusable lemma unimodal_of_palindrome_first_half_mono shows that for any nonnegative sequence supported on [0,d] and palindromic there, weak monotonicity across the first half (f j ≤ f (j+1) for 2j+2 ≤ d) already forces unimodality — the descending half is reconstructed by reflecting each rising step through the palindrome, and the central step of an odd-degree array is pinned by symmetry. Applied to the Gaussian polynomial (qBinomCoeff_unimodal_of_first_half_mono) this turns Sylvester's theorem for a fixed k into the single inequality coeff j ≤ coeff (j+1) on the first half.

**The k = 2 column is the first genuine bump, with an explicit ramp**: For k ≤ 1 the coefficient array is non-increasing (an indicator prefix), so unimodality is trivial. The k = 2 array of [n choose 2]_q is the first that truly rises then falls; its first half has the closed arithmetic form ⌊j/2⌋ + 1 (qBinom_X_two_coeff_le), derived from the coefficient recurrence coeff j = [j<n] + [2≤j]·(coeff at j−2). That explicit non-decreasing ramp feeds the palindrome criterion to give unimodality for every n — Approach C (small-k closed forms first) in action.

**Palindromy has an integral, coefficient-level form independent of the field**: The self-reciprocity qBinom_reciprocal lives over a field because it divides by q, but its coefficient shadow reflect (k(n-k)) (qBinom X n k) = qBinom X n k (qBinom_X_reflect) is proved over ℤ[X] with no inverses, by the same two-q-Pascal mechanism: reflecting the first Pascal expansion term-by-term (reflect_add, reflect_mul) yields exactly the second Pascal expansion. This is the form a_j = a_{k(n-k)−j} that actually composes with a coefficient-level unimodality argument.

sections.title: Open Question and Mathematical Context
sections.summary: Module docstring stating the target (palindromy of Gaussian q-binomials as the symmetric half of Sylvester's unimodality theorem), the proof outline via both q-Pascal identities, and an explicit honesty note that unimodality itself is NOT proved.

sections.title: Setup: namespace and the field hypothesis
sections.summary: Enters namespace QBinomialCoefficients, opens Nat, and fixes the ambient ring as an arbitrary field [Field R]. The field hypothesis is essential rather than cosmetic: the reciprocity identity substitutes q ↦ q⁻¹, so R must contain the inverse of every nonzero q — exactly what a field guarantees. This is the smallest setting in which the palindromy statement is even expressible.
sections.mathContext: R : Type* with [Field R]; needed so q⁻¹ exists for every q ≠ 0 in the reciprocity q ↦ q⁻¹.

sections.title: Main — Self-Reciprocity / Palindromy
sections.summary: qBinom_reciprocal: [n,k]_q = q^{k(n-k)}·[n,k]_{q⁻¹} over a field for q ≠ 0, by induction on n. Interior case k<n expands the left by qBinom_pascal' and the reflected right by qBinom_pascal, applies the induction hypothesis, and closes by the power cancellation q^{(k+1)(n-k)}·(q⁻¹)^{k+1} = q^{(k+1)(n-k-1)}; boundary/diagonal/vanishing cases are direct.

sections.title: Reflected Form and Involutivity
sections.summary: qBinom_reflect (the right-to-left convenience form q^{k(n-k)}·[n,k]_{q⁻¹} = [n,k]_q) and qBinom_reciprocal_involutive (applying the twisted reflection twice returns the original, confirming it is an involution as any palindrome reflection must be).

sections.title: The Gaussian polynomial over ℤ[X]: degree, monicity, coefficients
sections.summary: Specialising the ambient ring to ℤ[X] with q = X turns qBinom X n k into the Gaussian polynomial whose coefficient sequence Sylvester's theorem concerns. qBinom_X_monic_natDegree proves it monic of natDegree k·(n-k) by induction on q-Pascal (the X^{k+1}·qBinom X n (k+1) summand strictly dominates in degree when n-k ≥ 1, via degree_add_eq_left_of_degree_lt and Monic.add_of_left). qBinom_X_coeff_zero pins the constant term to 1 (the shifted summand contributes nothing at coefficient 0). qBinom_X_coeff_nonneg shows every coefficient is ≥ 0 over the ordered ring ℤ. The convenience corollaries qBinom_X_monic / qBinom_X_natDegree / qBinom_X_coeff_top and the capstone qBinom_X_extreme_coeffs pin both ends of the coefficient array to 1.
sections.mathContext: qBinom (X : ℤ[X]) n k : ℤ[X]; coeff_mul_X_pow', natDegree_mul, natDegree_X_pow, degree_lt_degree, Monic.add_of_left over the ordered ring ℤ.

sections.title: Coefficient palindromy over ℤ[X] (integral, no field)
sections.summary: Upgrades the field self-reciprocity qBinom_reciprocal to its integral, coefficient-level shadow with no field hypothesis. qBinom_X_reflect proves reflect (k(n-k)) (qBinom X n k) = qBinom X n k over ℤ[X] by induction on the q-Pascal recurrence: reflecting the FIRST Pascal expansion A + X^{k+1}·B term-by-term (reflect_add, reflect_mul) produces X^{n-k}·A + B, which is exactly the SECOND Pascal expansion qBinom_pascal' of the same polynomial — the ℤ[X] mirror of how the two q-Pascal identities matched the field proof. qBinom_X_coeff_symm reads this off as coeff j = coeff (revAt (k(n-k)) j), and qBinom_X_coeff_symm' gives the concrete symmetric array a_j = a_{k(n-k)−j} of Sylvester's theorem for j ≤ k(n-k).
sections.mathContext: Polynomial.reflect, reflect_add, reflect_mul, reflect_monomial, revAt_le, coeff_reflect; the integral coefficient-reversal a_j = a_{k(n-k)-j} that the field identity only implied via q⁻¹.

sections.title: Base change: naturality and specialization of the Gaussian polynomial
sections.summary: The q-binomial is assembled purely from ring operations of the q-Pascal recurrence, so it commutes with every ring homomorphism: qBinom_map proves f([n,k]_q) = [n,k]_{f q} by induction. Two specializations tie the polynomial layer back to scalars: qBinom_X_eval evaluates qBinom X n k at c ∈ ℤ (via evalRingHom c) to recover the scalar qBinom c n k, and qBinom_X_eval_one degenerates at q = 1 to the ordinary binomial C(n,k) — equivalently, the coefficients of the Gaussian polynomial sum to C(n,k), the q = 1 shadow at the root of the combinations-formula lineage.
sections.mathContext: RingHom naturality of qBinom; evalRingHom c, coe_evalRingHom, eval_X; qBinom_at_one giving eval 1 = C(n,k) = Σ coefficients.

sections.title: The Unimodal predicate and the general palindrome criterion
sections.summary: Mathlib has no unimodality predicate for integer sequences, so one is introduced: Unimodal f means there is a peak p below which f weakly increases and from which it weakly decreases. Unimodal.noValley recasts it in the problem's stated no-strict-valley form. Two elementary constructors (unimodal_of_nonincreasing, unimodal_const) handle degenerate arrays. The workhorse is unimodal_of_palindrome_first_half_mono: a nonnegative sequence supported on [0,d], palindromic there, and weakly increasing across its first half (f j ≤ f (j+1) for 2j+2 ≤ d) is unimodal with peak ⌊d/2⌋ — the falling half is reconstructed by reflecting each descending step through the palindrome, the central step of an odd array is forced by symmetry, and nonnegativity closes the boundary past the support. unimodal_of_even_palindrome_first_half_mono is the even-degree specialization used for k = 2.
sections.mathContext: Unimodal f := ∃ p, (∀ i<p, f i ≤ f (i+1)) ∧ (∀ i≥p, f (i+1) ≤ f i); reduces Sylvester's theorem for any k to weak monotonicity of the first half of a symmetric nonnegative array.

sections.title: Sylvester unimodality for k = 0 and k = 1 (non-increasing base cases)
sections.summary: Settles the base cases where the coefficient array is explicit. qNumber_eq_sum supplies the un-multiplied geometric form [n]_q = Σ_{i<n} qⁱ (the parent only had the (q−1)-multiplied identity), which lets qBinom_X_coeff_one_seq read the k = 1 coefficients as the indicator [j < n]. qBinomCoeff_unimodal_zero (array 1,0,0,… for [n,0]_q = 1) and qBinomCoeff_unimodal_one (array 1,…,1,0,… for [n,1]_q = [n]_q) are then both non-increasing, hence unimodal with peak at 0 (Approach C: small-k closed forms first).
sections.mathContext: qNumber_eq_sum, coeff_X_pow, Finset.sum_ite_eq; k ≤ 1 columns are non-increasing indicator arrays.

sections.title: Sylvester unimodality for k = 2 (first genuine rise-then-fall bump)
sections.summary: The first column that genuinely rises AND falls. qBinom_X_two_coeff_succ derives the coefficient recurrence coeff j = [j<n] + [2≤j]·(previous coeff at j−2) from qBinom_pascal at k = 1. qBinom_X_two_coeff_le then solves the first half in closed form: for n = m+2 and j ≤ m, coeff j = ⌊j/2⌋ + 1, a manifestly non-decreasing arithmetic ramp. Feeding this ramp plus the established coefficient palindromy and nonnegativity into unimodal_of_even_palindrome_first_half_mono yields qBinomCoeff_unimodal_two for every n (with n < 2 giving the zero polynomial). This settles Sylvester's theorem for k = 2.
sections.mathContext: First-half closed form (qBinom X (m+2) 2).coeff j = ⌊j/2⌋+1 for j ≤ m; even degree 2m; Nat.div_le_div_right for monotonicity of the ramp.

sections.title: The general reduction: unimodality ⇐ first-half monotonicity (all n, k)
sections.summary: Packages the structural facts so that Sylvester's theorem for any fixed k reduces to a single inequality. qBinomCoeff_unimodal_of_first_half_mono shows that for k ≤ n, if the coefficient sequence of [n,k]_q is weakly increasing across its first half (coeff j ≤ coeff (j+1) whenever 2j+2 ≤ k(n−k)), then it is unimodal — the falling half, central step, and tail are all supplied by unimodal_of_palindrome_first_half_mono from the already-proved nonnegativity, degree, and palindromy. This is the reusable reduction on which the k = 2 proof was built and toward which any future general-k (O'Hara / 𝔰𝔩₂) argument need only supply the first-half inequality.
sections.mathContext: qBinomCoeff_unimodal_of_first_half_mono: symmetric + nonnegative + supported-on-[0,k(n-k)] ⇒ unimodality follows from first-half weak monotonicity alone.

sections.title: Toward k = 3: the coefficient recurrence and box-free prefix monotonicity
sections.summary: Opens the k = 3 column, the first case where the box constraint 'each part ≤ n−k' genuinely binds inside the first half. Two theorems are supplied. qBinom_X_three_coeff_succ is the k = 3 coefficient recurrence: from the q-Pascal identity [n+1,3]_q = [n,2]_q + q³·[n,3]_q, the coefficient array of [n+1,3]_q equals the [n,2]_q array plus the q³-shifted [n,3]_q array, i.e. coeff j = ([n,2]_q).coeff j + [3 ≤ j]·([n,3]_q).coeff (j−3). qBinom_X_three_coeff_prefix_mono then settles the box-free prefix: writing the box as 3 × N (n = N + 3, degree 3N), the coefficient sequence of [N+3,3]_q is weakly increasing across j + 1 ≤ N, the range where the constraint 'each part ≤ N' does not yet bind. The proof is a clean induction on N through the recurrence — the [n,2] increment is ≥ 0 there (the k = 2 ramp ⌊j/2⌋+1) and the shifted [n,3] increment is ≥ 0 by the induction hypothesis (or trivially for j < 3). At the time this section was written the box-binding tail N < j ≤ ⌊(3N−2)/2⌋ — where a naive n-induction turns negative past the [n,2] peak — was left open; it is closed in the following sections by a different, second-form recurrence, not by the 𝔰𝔩₂/O'Hara machinery anticipated here.
sections.mathContext: q-Pascal at k = 2: [n+1,3]_q = [n,2]_q + q³·[n,3]_q, giving coeff j = ([n,2]_q).coeff j + (if 3 ≤ j then ([n,3]_q).coeff (j−3) else 0). Box-free prefix (j + 1 ≤ N, n = N + 3): both increments ≥ 0, so induction on N gives coeff j ≤ coeff (j+1). The box-binding tail N < j ≤ ⌊(3N−2)/2⌋ is closed later in this file (see 'Closing the k = 3 box-binding tail').

sections.title: High-Codimension Cases k ≥ n − 2 via the Symmetry [n,k]_q = [n,n−k]_q
sections.summary: qBinomCoeff_unimodal_of_codim_le_two: Sylvester's theorem is symmetric under k ↦ n−k because the Gaussian polynomials there are literally equal (qBinom_symm — choosing k from n is choosing n−k). Rewriting by this symmetry transports the already-proved base cases k = 0, 1, 2 to every k with n − k ≤ 2, closing an infinite family of high-codimension columns (k ∈ {n−2, n−1, n} for every n) at no extra analytic cost, so that the only range left open after this section is the genuine interior 3 ≤ k ≤ n − 3.
sections.mathContext: qBinom_symm : [n,k]_q = [n,n−k]_q; rw by this identity plus case split on n − k ∈ {0,1,2} reduces to qBinomCoeff_unimodal_{zero,one,two}.

sections.title: Closing the k = 3 Box-Binding Tail: the Second-Form Recurrence and Reflection Pairs
sections.summary: Introduces the mechanism that closes the k = 3 tail elementarily. The docstring explains the idea: the SECOND q-Pascal form [N+4,3]_q = [N+3,3]_q + q^{N+1}·[N+3,2]_q (qBinom_X_three_coeff_succ') writes the box-3×(N+1) increment as the box-3×N increment plus the *exactly known* k = 2 ramp (⌊j/2⌋+1), and the first half of box 3×(N+1) extends past that of box 3×N by at most two 'center-band' indices. qBinom_X_three_center_pair, qBinom_X_three_outer_pair, and qBinom_X_three_even_pair read off the palindromy reflections needed at those indices; qBinom_X_three_band_O_zero computes the M = 0 base case explicitly ([4,3]_q = 1+q+q²+q³); qBinom_X_three_band_E2_of_O propagates the odd-box zero increment forward to give the even-box increment as an exact ramp-parity value [M odd].
sections.mathContext: Second q-Pascal form: [N+4,3]_q = [N+3,3]_q + q^{N+1}·[N+3,2]_q. Center-band base case: odd box 3×(2M+1) has increment 0 at its band point; even box 3×(2M+2) increment is the ramp parity [M odd]/[M even].

sections.title: The Center-Band Recursion: qBinom_X_three_band
sections.summary: qBinom_X_three_band proves, by mutual induction on M, the full center-band recursion: the odd-box band increment is always exactly 0, and the even-box band increment is always exactly the ramp parity [M odd]. The two claims feed each other (odd-box at M+1 needs even-box at M via the even-degree reflection pair; even-box at M needs odd-box at M). qBinom_X_three_band_E1 supplies the remaining even-box first band increment ([M even]) via the pure-palindromy center pair. Together these three theorems pin every center-band increment of the k = 3 array to exactly 0 or 1 — the quantitative control across the [n,2]-ramp peak that the first-form recurrence could not provide.
sections.mathContext: Mutual induction: band(M).odd = 0, band(M).even = [M odd]; qBinom_X_three_band_E1 gives the companion even-box first increment [M even]. All center-band increments are exactly 0 or 1.

sections.title: Sylvester's Theorem CLOSED for k = 3 (and Codimension ≤ 3)
sections.summary: Assembles the pieces into the full result. qBinom_X_three_coeff_first_half_mono proves first-half monotonicity for k = 3 UNCONDITIONALLY (every N, every j in the first half): below the previous box's midpoint the increment is the induction hypothesis plus a nonnegative ramp step, and at the (at most two) center-band indices the increment is the exact 0/1 value from qBinom_X_three_band — this is exactly the range N < j ≤ ⌊(3N−2)/2⌋ that qBinom_X_three_coeff_prefix_mono left open. qBinomCoeff_unimodal_three then feeds this into the general reduction to prove Sylvester's theorem for k = 3 for every n, with NO 𝔰𝔩₂-action or O'Hara decomposition. Finally qBinomCoeff_unimodal_of_codim_le_three combines this with the codimension-≤-2 symmetry result to cover every k ≤ 3 or k ≥ n − 3, narrowing Sylvester's open range in this development to the genuine interior 4 ≤ k ≤ n − 4 (first open instance: [8,4]_q).
sections.mathContext: qBinom_X_three_coeff_first_half_mono: coeff j ≤ coeff (j+1) for all 2j+2 ≤ 3N, unconditionally. qBinomCoeff_unimodal_three: Sylvester's theorem for k = 3, all n. qBinomCoeff_unimodal_of_codim_le_three: k ≤ 3 ∨ k ≥ n−3 ⇒ unimodal; open range now 4 ≤ k ≤ n−4.

conclusion.summary: A self-contained, axiom-free Lean file (43 theorems, 1 definition) that establishes the Gaussian q-binomial coefficient [n,k]_q is palindromic — in the clean field form [n,k]_q = q^{k(n-k)}·[n,k]_{q⁻¹} (for q ≠ 0) and integrally over ℤ[X] as a coefficient reversal a_j = a_{k(n-k)−j} via Polynomial.reflect — and then advances substantially into the unimodal half of Sylvester's 1878 theorem: it introduces a Unimodal predicate, a general reduction (qBinomCoeff_unimodal_of_first_half_mono) collapsing Sylvester's theorem for any fixed k to weak monotonicity of the array's first half, proves unimodality unconditionally for k = 0, 1, 2, and extends that to every codimension n − k ≤ 2 via the symmetry [n,k]_q = [n,n−k]_q. It then closes k = 3 completely: a second q-Pascal form yields an exact 0/1 'center-band' recursion that tracks the coefficient increments across the box-binding peak a naive induction cannot cross, giving unconditional first-half monotonicity for k = 3 (qBinom_X_three_coeff_first_half_mono) and hence Sylvester's theorem for k = 3 (qBinomCoeff_unimodal_three) with NO 𝔰𝔩₂-representation theory or O'Hara decomposition. Combined with the codimension-≤-2 result, Sylvester's theorem is now proved for every k ≤ 3 or k ≥ n − 3; the open range has narrowed to the genuine interior 4 ≤ k ≤ n − 4.
conclusion.implications: Palindromy is exactly the piece of Sylvester's theorem that is elementary, and isolating it cleanly turns the open unimodality question into 'a symmetric sequence is unimodal'. The k = 3 closure additionally shows that at least one interior column defeats the box constraint by pure parity bookkeeping rather than representation theory — evidence that the general-k first-half inequality may admit more elementary approaches than the 𝔰𝔩₂/O'Hara route, even though no such approach is known yet for k ≥ 4. The palindromy identity also encodes the geometric duality between k-dimensional subspaces of 𝔽_qⁿ and their (n−k)-dimensional annihilators (which reverses the q-grading), and it is the q-analogue of the ordinary binomial symmetry C(n,k) = C(n,n−k) recovered at q = 1.
openQuestions: Unimodality of the coefficient sequence of [n,k]_q for the genuine INTERIOR range 4 ≤ k ≤ n − 4 — the remaining substantive content of Sylvester's theorem after this file closes k ≤ 3 and k ≥ n − 3. The general reduction qBinomCoeff_unimodal_of_first_half_mono still applies, so what is needed is first-half monotonicity for k = 4, 5, … ; the only known proofs for general k use an 𝔰𝔩₂-action (Proctor 1982) or an explicit injection between adjacent coefficient levels (O'Hara 1990). Concrete next step: attempt k = 4 by the same center-band strategy that closed k = 3 (a third q-Pascal form or a two-step ramp correction), since [8,4]_q is the first genuinely open instance.

Does the k = 3 center-band technique generalize to a uniform argument for all k, or does the band width / ramp complexity grow with k in a way that forces the 𝔰𝔩₂/O'Hara machinery past some threshold? Characterizing exactly where the elementary approach stops working would clarify how much of Sylvester's theorem is 'really' representation-theoretic.
Formalize the subspace-counting interpretation, deriving palindromy from the bijection between k- and (n−k)-dimensional subspaces of 𝔽_qⁿ instead of from the recurrence.

references.title: Proof of the hitherto undemonstrated fundamental theorem of invariants
references.note: Philosophical Magazine. Establishes that the coefficient sequence of the Gaussian binomial is symmetric and unimodal; the symmetry (palindromy) half is what is formalized here.

references.title: Solution of two difficult combinatorial problems with linear algebra
references.note: American Mathematical Monthly 89(10). The first fully rigorous proof of unimodality via an sl₂ (raising/lowering operator) action — the open half of the result.

references.title: Unimodality of Gaussian coefficients: a constructive proof
references.note: Journal of Combinatorial Theory, Series A 53(1). A purely combinatorial (injection-based) proof of unimodality, avoiding representation theory.

references.title: The Theory of Partitions
references.note: Encyclopedia of Mathematics and its Applications, Cambridge University Press. Standard reference for Gaussian binomials, q-Pascal recurrences, and their symmetry as generating functions for partitions in a box.

references.title: Quantum Calculus
references.note: Springer Universitext. Develops q-binomial coefficients and the two q-Pascal rules used here as the engine of the palindromy induction.

crossReferences.description: Parent. Defines the q-binomial coefficient over an arbitrary commutative ring via the q-Pascal recurrence and proves BOTH q-Pascal identities (qBinom_pascal, qBinom_pascal') plus the vanishing lemma qBinom_eq_zero_of_lt — exactly the toolkit this file inducts with to prove palindromy.
Grandparent. The ordinary binomial coefficient and its symmetry C(n,k) = C(n,n−k); palindromy of the q-binomial is the q-analogue that degenerates to this classical symmetry at q = 1.
The classical binomial theorem, whose coefficients are the q = 1 specialization of the Gaussian binomials studied here; the q-Pascal recurrences reduce to ordinary Pascal's rule at q = 1.
